location: workspace/solution.py: sample_step() schedule reads + time embedding; sample() per-crystal loop
why: The baseline reads noise-schedule scalars back to the host with .item() each step, rebuilds the sinusoidal time embedding from many tiny tensor operations each step, and samples the eval batch one crystal at a time. Pre-computing schedule tensors on device, vectorising/fusing the time embedding, and batching the loop removes most of the host/Python overhead without changing the sampler math.
